quotes.quote: Multiply matching coordinates, sum their products and add the bias: the logit is minus one.
Sigmoid is one divided by the quantity one plus exponential of negative logit.

For binary cross-entropy from one sigmoid logit, the logit gradient is probability minus target. Here that is approximately minus point seven three one one. Each weight gradient multiplies that value by its feature coordinate; the bias gradient is the same logit gradient.
Subtract learning rate point one times each gradient.

answers.reason: Initially z=0 and p=.5. The logit gradient is .5, weight gradient is .5×−2=−1, and bias gradient is .5. SGD gives weight .10 and bias −.05; the new logit is .10×−2−.05=−.25.

quotes.quote: Sigmoid is one divided by the quantity one plus exponential of negative logit.

Binary cross-entropy for an observed category is negative target times log probability, minus the quantity one minus target multiplied by log of the quantity one minus probability. Mask unknown entries, sum only observed losses, then divide by the number observed.
Their mean is one point four one zero zero; the unknown contributes no loss or gradient.
With this mean, each observed logit gradient is its probability minus target, divided by two.

answers.reason: Each observed zero logit gives probability .5 and loss ln(2), so their mean is ln(2). Dividing observed gradients by two gives [−.25, 0, .25, 0].
